chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithami, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-A'la, the freedman of the family of Sam, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'On the Day of Resurrection, a beautiful woman will be brought forward who had been tested (fitnat) due to her beauty. She will say: "O Lord, You made my creation beautiful until I encountered what I encountered." Then Maryam (peace be upon her) will be brought, and it will be said to her: "Are you more beautiful, or her? We made her beautiful, but she was not tested (did not fall into sin)."'

And a handsome man who had been tested due to his beauty will be brought, and he will say: "O Lord, You made my creation handsome until I encountered from the women what I encountered." Then Yusuf (peace be upon him) will be brought, and it will be said to him: "Are you more handsome, or this one? We made him handsome, but he was not tested (did not fall into sin)."'

And the owner of affliction, upon whom the trial had befallen in his affliction, will be brought, and he will say: "O Lord, You intensified the affliction upon me until I was tested (fell into sin)." Then Ayyub (peace be upon him) will be brought, and it will be said: "Is your affliction more severe, or his affliction? He was tested, but he was not tested (did not fall into sin)."'

key_terms.افْتُتِنَتْ: She was tested/tempted and fell into sin
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةُ: Trial, test, or temptation leading to sin

ai.seo_question: How does Islam explain the relationship between physical beauty, affliction, and sin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle that physical beauty and severe trials are merely tests, not excuses, by contrasting ordinary sinners with the archetypal models of patience and chastity: Maryam, Yusuf, and Ayyub. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, emphasizes that while these figures possessed superior attributes or endured greater hardships, their steadfastness (sabr) in the face of fitnah serves as the ultimate benchmark for divine judgment. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the capacity to resist temptation is a matter of spiritual discipline rather than external circumstance.

en.hubeali: H 14739 – Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad Al-Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al-Hassan Al-Maysamy, from Aban Bin usman, from Abdul A’la a slave of progeny of Saam who said: I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘On the Day of Judgement, they will bring a beautiful woman who had done Fitna (mischief) due to her beauty. So she will say, ‘O Lordazwj! Youazwj Created me beautiful until I did what I did. So they will come with Maryamas and say to her, ‘Are you more beautiful or heras? Sheas had beauty in heras but did not do Fitna (mischief)’. And they would come with the handsome man who had done Fitna (mischief) due to his beauty. So he will say, ‘O Lordazwj! Youazwj Created me with beauty until I did with the women what I did. So they will bring Yusufas and say, ‘Are you more handsome or heas is? Heas had beauty but did not do Fitna (mischief)’. And they will come with the afflicted person who had been involved in Ftina (mischief) due to his afflictions. So he will say, ‘O Lordazwj! The intensity of the afflictions upon me were such that I did Fitna (mischief)’. So they would come with Ayyubas. So they would say, ‘Were your afflictions more severe or hisas afflictions? Heas was in afflictions but did not do Fitna (mischief)’.
en.sarwar: 291. Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al-Hassan Bin Muhammad Al-Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al-Hassan Al-Maysamy, from Aban Bin usman, from Abdul A’la a slave of progeny of Saam who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘On the Day of Judgement, they will bring a beautiful woman who had done Fitna (mischief) due to her beauty. So she will say, ‘O Lord (azwj)! You (azwj) Created me beautiful until I did what I did. So they will come with Maryam (as) and say to her, ‘Are you more beautiful or her (as)? She (as) had beauty in her (as) but did not do Fitna (mischief)’.

And they would come with the handsome man who had done Fitna (mischief) due to his beauty. So he will say, ‘O Lord (azwj)! You (azwj) Created me with beauty until I did with the women what I did. So they will bring Yusuf (as) and say, ‘Are you more handsome or he (as) is? He (as) had beauty but did not do Fitna (mischief)’.

And they will come with the afflicted person who had been involved in Ftina (mischief) due to his afflictions. So he will say, ‘O Lord (azwj)! The intensity of the afflictions upon me were such that I did Fitna (mischief)’. So they would come with Ayyub (as). So they would say, ‘Were your afflictions more severe or his (as) afflictions? He (as) was in afflictions but did not do Fitna (mischief)’.
